title: Folding buys an additive-energy reduction: the (d+1)-orbit fold is the multiplicative analogue of the 2-adic char-sum descent (W-subspace and W-BGK share one deflation mechanism)
evidence: Exact probes at PROPER-subgroup primes (q = 1 mod n, n << sqrt q, beta = ln q/ln n ~ 4.0): scripts/probes/_407_conn/C038_deflation_compare.py and C038_descent_bound_check.py. Computed M(n) = max_{b!=0} |sum_{y in mu_n} e_q(by)| (Gauss-period sup-norm = non-principal Paley eigenvalue) for the genuine multiplicative subgroup mu_n and its x->x^2 image mu_{n/2}, exactly, n=8,16,32,64 over multiple primes each. (1) The alleged char-sum descent bound M(n)^2 <= 2*M(n/2)^2 (F8, the claimed multiplicative analogue of the orbit fold) is FALSE in the prize regime: R = M(n)^2/M(n/2)^2 = 3.69 (n=8), 2.84-2.99 (n=16), 2.47-2.69 (n=32), 2.24 (n=64) -- ABOVE 2 in ALL 9 cases (bound fails 9/9). (2) R is NOT a fixed factor 2: it drifts monotonically with n and is reproduced to 4 decimals by the BGK-law decomposition R = 2*(c(n)/c(n/2))^2 * log(q/n)/log(2q/n), where c(n) = M(n)/sqrt(n log(q/n)) is STABLE (~1.03-1.33, the documented BGK signature 0.9-1.1). So the '2' inside M^2/M(n/2)^2 is the trivial n -> 2*(n/2) size doubling inside sqrt(n*log), present for ANY size-doubling subgroup and unrelated to the x->x^2 ORBIT structure. (3) The orbit-fold deflation (d+1)*foldedAgree <= plainAgree (FoldingTransferNoGo.lean, axiom-clean) is by contrast an EXACT lossless INTEGER combinatorial inequality, provable for any 2-to-1 fold over any field, independent of cancellation, with converse failing maximally. The two 'factor-2 deflations' are categorically different objects; the connection's central claim of a SHARED deflation mechanism is refuted. The hard open content of W-BGK is the constant c(n) (= the BGK sqrt-cancellation), about which the orbit fold says nothing. This is the connection's own attack_plan 'diverge -> two-walls framing CONFIRMED' branch, plus a sharper bonus refutation: the F8 descent inequality M(n)^2 <= 2 M(n/2)^2 is itself false at proper subgroups.
honest_note: Probes run at dyadic n=8..64 with beta ~ 4 (n << sqrt q), not the literal prize n=2^30; q kept tractable (work ~ q) so n=128+ not run. The refutation is structural and uniform across the tested range: it rests on the well-established stability of c(n)=M/sqrt(n log) (BGK law, consistent with the KB's documented B/sqrt(n log(p/n)) ~ 0.9-1.1) and on M(n)^2/M(n/2)^2 being an analytic BGK size-doubling ratio rather than the lossless integer orbit factor. I refuted the LOAD-BEARING claim (shared mechanism) and the F8 descent bound as stated; I did not (and cannot) settle the underlying BGK cancellation itself, which remains the genuine 25-year-open core. The two walls do NOT collapse into one deflation Prop. Should go to DISPROOF_LOG.
